main_issue: How to pay for soft drinks and snacks now that the house fund was spent entirely on alcohol, and whether the cost split is fair to non-drinkers.

A-B.evidence: A accepts B's point about soft drinks (T3); B's funding question (T12) is met by A's defense of the alcohol (T11), with no resolution.

A-C.evidence: C questions the cost and notes the fund is empty (T5-7); A answers factually (T6) but never responds to C's $10 split (T13) or to C's later concession to D.

A-D.evidence: D calls the all-alcohol spend unfair (T8, T10); A defends it: 'That's just what the alcohol cost' and 'Our guests will want drinks' (T9, T11); A never responds to D's proposal in T16.

B-C.evidence: C tells B the soft drinks can't come from the fund (T7), then proposes an equal $10 split to answer B's question (T13); C later retracts it for D's view (T15), and B is silent.

B-D.evidence: B wanted soft drinks for non-drinkers (T2) and asks how to pay (T12); D wants drinkers to cover soft drinks (T16). They are broadly compatible, but B never responds directly.

C-D.evidence: D objects to C's $10-each plan as unfair (T14); C concedes 'You're right, that's not fair' and asks D for a fair way (T15); D proposes drinkers cover soft drinks (T16).
